published_prior_art.cite: KennedyHarrisKeele2019 and DongHeiler2026 identify/bound survivor-complier mean targets, not same-unit ordinal-coupling capacities.
DongHeiler2026 supplies weak direction partitions for trimmed mean bounds, but not the direction-invariant fixed-marginal transport face at an observable tie.

repo_prior_art.cite: No catalogue entry duplicates a sharp survivor-complier ordinal-benefit interval under IV noncompliance and treatment-induced selection.

published_prior_art.cite: LuDingDasgupta2018 gives fixed-marginal ordinal-benefit bounds; GabrielSachsJensen2024 gives full-population IV benefit bounds without selection; deAguasEtAl2025 gives ignorability-based tier-benefit bounds. None covers unequal survivor-complier submargins.
The cited ordinal-benefit papers establish their own sharpness constructions, but none supplies the proposed completion from an unequal survivor-complier subcoupling to a full IV-selection law.
GabrielSachsJensen2024 computes symbolic bounds for finite ordinal IV models, but does not give a magnitude-independent threshold-flow algorithm for the survivor-complier partial-transport problem.
ChenFlores2015 supplies the Job Corps mean-bound setting, not this explicit ordinal same-unit-benefit IV-selection witness.
LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), already gives the fixed-marginal strict-benefit formula; this result is the appropriate reduction check for the new model.
FangSantos2019 provides generic directional-delta theory and deAguasEtAl2025 treats a different tier-benefit functional; neither derives this projected-capacity, screened-ratio composite limit.
FangSantos2019, ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013, Semenova2025, and deAguasEtAl2025 leave the stated joint changing-support two-endpoint coverage problem unresolved.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Results 3-4; journal HTML lines 140-163.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives tight valid bounds for the full-population probability of benefit in its IV/noncompliance DAG for K=3,...,7, with and without no defiers; it does not include treatment-induced outcome selection or a survivor-complier target.

source_verification_receipts.version: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 275 (2025), conference proceedings version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Under conditional ignorability and positivity, the paper gives sharp tiered-benefit bounds with and without strong monotonicity, and subsequently studies nonregular inference; its setting has complete treatment-arm outcome information rather than IV-identified survivor-complier submeasures.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1507.01542v3 (accepted-version corroboration; cited journal text was not publicly inspectable)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 2 gives sharp lower and upper bounds for the strict-benefit probability under fixed ordinal marginals. This corroborates the proposal's intended no-selection reduction and is not used to make an adverse source-mismatch finding.

The paper studies sharp partial identification and inference for intensive-margin treatment effects among compliers under weak sample-selection monotonicity and endogenous treatment, rather than an ordinal same-unit benefit coupling.

source_verification_receipts.version: Pre-publication version of Generalized Lee Bounds; journal metadata confirmed at DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106055
source_verification_receipts.locator: Pages 9-10, Assumptions 2-3; page 15, Remark 3 and equation (4.17).
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper formulates covariate-specific selection directions, treats the zero-direction boundary, and explicitly records fixed positive sign separation as plausible for discrete covariates. It supports the proposal's use of a direction-margin condition only for its inference subclass.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 114(525) (2019), pp. 93-104; published-version repository record

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article derives sharp bounds and efficient estimation methods for a survivor-complier causal effect under treatment-induced selection; its target is a mean effect rather than ordinal same-unit benefit probability.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a formal strict-separation corollary comparing the survivor-complier interval with GabrielSachsJensen2024's full-population IV interval on a displayed common submodel, including an observable law on which the two targets or bounds differ.

Turn the uniform face-aware multiplier question into a concrete theorem target by specifying admissible rates for a_n and eta_n and a conditional critical-value functional, initially under a fixed finite covariate support.
Extend the attainment construction to a jointly sharp vector of benefit, no-harm, and large-gain tier events, rather than treating each threshold separately.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0: make the general endpoint-preserving full-law completion the first proof obligation, then verify the threshold-flow formulas against the specified three-level witness and finite latent-type LPs.
